name: Cereflux
description: Cereflux is an anti-neuroinflammatory compound formulated specifically for BCI-associated cerebral edema — the swelling and microtrauma caused by sustained high-bandwidth neural-digital interface activity. It combines a targeted blood-brain barrier permeant anti-inflammatory with glymphatic drainage enhancers to clear inflammatory metabolites from neural tissue. Standard issue for anyone in a high-BCI-load profession.
effects: relieves BCI headache and cognitive fog
lowers risk of chronic neuroinflammation from extended BCI sessions
mild analgesic effect at neural interface sites
side_effects: reduced BCI bandwidth during active dose
low blood pressure in some users
cultural_context: Cereflux is the ibuprofen of the BCI age. Anyone who spends long hours jacked into high-bandwidth work — data laborers, operators, coders, corporate analysts — keeps a strip of Cereflux in their kit. The Tier 2 working class calls it 'head drain' because it feels like pressure releasing. Overuse is common and quietly encouraged by employers who'd rather workers dose up than log off.
story_hooks: A corporate analyst discovers that the Cereflux supplied by their employer contains a compound that subtly degrades BCI security protocols over time
A the Gray Zone community is experiencing epidemic neuroinflammation — their only source of Cereflux is diluted counterfeit stock
A character's Cereflux has stopped working — their neuroinflammation is worsening despite dosing, and imaging reveals something growing around their BCI implant
